description: EDA of Dataset 1 (Sentiment Analysis for Mental Health, 53,043 posts): bar chart of the seven raw class labels showing strong imbalance — Normal (16,351) and Depression (15,404) dominate while Personality disorder (1,201) and Stress (2,669) are rare, motivating label unification and class-weighted training.

EDA of Dataset 1: distribution of post lengths (words per post) showing a long right tail; the bulk of posts fit within a 128-token window, which was adopted as the sequence length for all deep learning and transformer models.

EDA of Dataset 2 (Depression Reddit Cleaned, 7,731 posts): bar chart of the binary labels showing a nearly balanced split — Depression (3,831) vs Non-Depression (3,900), the latter mapped to the Normal class during merging.
EDA of Dataset 2: distribution of post lengths for the Reddit depression dataset, used together with Dataset 1 lengths to choose the 128-token input limit.

Grouped bar chart comparing accuracy and macro-F1 of all six models on the held-out test set (n = 7,106): fine-tuned BERT leads (83.4% / 0.841), followed by XGBoost, Logistic Regression, CNN, frozen BERT and BiLSTM.
Radar chart of the same six-model comparison (accuracy and macro-F1 axes), giving a compact visual of how far the fine-tuned BERT extends beyond every baseline.

Row-normalised confusion matrix of the fine-tuned BERT on the test set: cleanest diagonal of all models; the dominant residual error is the clinically overlapping Depression ↔ Suicidal pair, while Normal is almost perfectly separated (F1 0.953).

Row-normalised confusion matrix of XGBoost (TF-IDF features) on the test set — the strongest classical baseline (77.2% accuracy); shows heavier Depression ↔ Suicidal confusion than the fine-tuned BERT.
Row-normalised confusion matrix of Logistic Regression (TF-IDF features) on the test set (76.7% accuracy), performing close to XGBoost with a similar error pattern.
Row-normalised confusion matrix of the CNN text classifier on the test set (73.3% accuracy), the stronger of the two deep learning baselines.
Row-normalised confusion matrix of the BiLSTM on the test set (64.1% accuracy), the weakest model in the comparison, with substantial confusion across the mental-health classes.
CNN training curves: training loss and validation metrics per epoch, used to monitor convergence and select the training budget for the CNN baseline.
BiLSTM training curves: training loss and validation metrics per epoch, showing slower and weaker convergence than the CNN.

Global SHAP token importance for the fine-tuned BERT: mean absolute SHAP value per token per class, aggregated over a stratified sample of 100 test posts (20 per class); surfaces the clinically salient vocabulary each class relies on.
Five SHAP explanations from the fine-tuned BERT — one correctly predicted test post per class — showing which tokens pushed the probability toward (green) or away from (red) the predicted class.
Five LIME explanations from the fine-tuned BERT — the same one-post-per-class examples — showing word-level weights from LIME's local linear surrogate for the predicted class.

Side-by-side SHAP and LIME explanation of the identical depression-related example text through the same fine-tuned BERT, illustrating that both methods highlight overlapping evidence (e.g. 'hopeless', 'pointless') while differing in granularity (sub-word spans vs whole words).
